messages:
Anya: Pushing a quick proposal for a lattice-based sample selection ablation for speculative decoding. TL;DR: instead of single draft beam, maintain small lattice of short drafts and score continuation candidates to decide early commit. Want to test latency vs quality tradeoffs.

Matt R: Sounds interesting — how small is "small" for the lattice? 4 drafts? 8?

Anya: Thinking 3-5 drafts initially. Keep per-step overhead minimal so we can measure real latency impact on our runtime.

Zhu: How does this differ from staged sampling / multi-pass that we already tried?

Anya: Good Q. Key diff: we keep the KV cache shared but track a lattice of draft prefixes with divergence flags. Decisions to speculatively commit use a lightweight scorer (quantized LM head) not a full re-rerank. So cheaper than full re-rank.

Sara P: Can you sketch the eval plan? Which datasets + metrics?

Anya: Plan: (1) Throughput and p50/p95 latency on our inference harness (single-GPU, batch=1); (2) Quality on a small curated eval set: 200 prompts across code, assistance, and summarization; metrics: exact-match / ROUGE / self-consistency score + targeted safety checks. Also measure token-redispatch overhead and fallback rate.

Noah S: For fairness, include a baseline: greedy, top-k draft (k=4) simple ensemble, and speculative oracle (perfect scorer) to bound.

Anya: Yep. Also include 8-bit quantized scorer vs fp16 to see scorer regression.

Matt R: Do we need model changes or just runtime orchestration?

Anya: Runtime only. We'll add a small scorer binary that loads weights in q4/8 format. No model retrain.

Zhu: I can run a quick microbench on GPU to measure per-step scorer cost. What command do you want me to run?

Anya: Thanks — use this harness command: 
```
./run_spec_ablation --model rwl-13b --lattice-size 4 --scorer q4 --batch 1 --send-trace=1 --prompts-file eval/200-mix.json
```
Collect p50/p95 lat, tokens/sec, and "commits_before_fallback".

Zhu: Running now on g0. I'll drop numbers in ~20m.

(eval-bot): quick-run started: job_id=spec-lattice-1715009999-zhu on g0. logs -> https://ci.internal/jobs/1715009999

Zhu: Raw first pass: p50=78ms p95=210ms tokens/sec=14.3 commits_before_fallback=0.72 scorer_cost=4.6ms per-step (q4). Baseline greedy p95=145ms tokens/sec=12.1. So lattice adds overhead but lowers decoding iterations (fewer re-rolls).

Anya: Interesting — p95 got worse but tokens/sec improved. Any quality numbers?

Zhu: Quick ROUGE-L on the 200 prompts: lattice=0.76, greedy=0.74, top-k-ensemble=0.77. Safety/degeneracy checks: no big regressions.

Sara P: That delta looks promising for token-efficiency. Can we tune lattice-size and scoring temp to reduce p95?

Anya: We'll sweep lattice-size {2,3,4,6} and scorer-temp {0.7,1.0,1.2}. Hypothesis: smaller lattice reduces worst-case p95; warmer scorer reduces over-commit and fallback.

Noah S: Add an experiment to count "late fallback" events (commit changed after step N) to understand instability.

Anya: Good call. We'll log commit-change-step histogram.

Matt R: Also run on dedicated 8-bit kernel (different kernel selection) — sometimes our p95 spikes due to kernel launch patterns.

Zhu: Noted. Will add dedicated-8bit run.

Anya: Next actions: 1) Zhu runs full sweep and uploads CSV to /mnt/evals/spec-lattice/1715009999/, 2) Sara prepares small write-up for eng-ml with plots (latency vs rouge, fallback rate), 3) Noah adds telemetry counters to runtime for commit-change histogram.

Sara P: I'll handle the write-up after Zhu's sweep. Planning to include short move-summary and a few plots.

(eval-bot): job spec-lattice-1715009999-zhu finished. artifacts: /ci/artifacts/spec-lattice/1715009999/results.tgz

Zhu: Sweep submitted. ETA ~2h. I pushed a mini-parse script to /tools/spec-lattice/parse_results.py.

Anya: Thanks team. If results look good we can fold the scorer into the staged speculative pipeline as an opt-in flag. If regressions show up we'll pivot to smaller lattice. :thumbsup:

Matt R: Awesome. Ping me if you need faster kernel experiments, I can attach a dedicated node.

Noah S: Also let's add a small unit test that asserts fallback rate < 0.15 for baseline config to prevent silent regressions.

Anya: Will add test. Closing for now; follow-up in ~3h when sweep completes.
